### OBL-013 — District web and mobile accessibility conformance to WCAG 2.1 AA

| Field              | Value                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | U.S. Department of Justice (SRC-017)                                                     |
| Authority type     | regulation                                                                               |
| Citation           | 28 CFR 35.200(b)                                                                         |
| Locator            | https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/04/24/2024-07758                          |
| Source version     | Final rule 2024, dates extended by 2026 interim final rule                               |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                               |
| Jurisdiction       | US-FEDERAL                                                                               |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-AT-PILOT                                                                         |
| Trigger            | A public entity uses SSLS as part of its web content or mobile services.                 |
| Control family     | ACCESSIBILITY                                                                            |
| Control status     | PARTIAL                                                                                  |
| Evidence status    | STALE                                                                                    |
| Owning route       | Accessibility validation work package                                                    |
| Review requirement | ACCESSIBILITY REVIEW REQUIRED                                                            |
| Review trigger     | Before any accessibility statement is published or any procurement response is submitted |

**What the source states.** The regulated party is the public entity. The rule does not regulate private vendors.

**Obligation.** Public entities must make web content and mobile applications conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, subject to listed exceptions and limited defences.

**SSLS interpretation.** Because the customer's duty is dated and non-negotiable, SSLS treats WCAG conformance as a product requirement now rather than a procurement surprise later. SSLS builds to WCAG 2.2 AA, which is a superset of the 2.1 AA criteria named in the rule.

**Current phase.** Not directly applicable. SSLS is not a public entity. The obligation reaches SSLS only through a district's own duty and its procurement terms.

**Future phase.** Districts must conform by 2027-04-26 for populations of fifty thousand or more, and 2028-04-26 for smaller populations and special district governments.

**Required control.** Verified conformance testing against the named criteria, with the internal target stated as a version.

**Current control.** ULW-AS-001 v1.3 internal standard applied across the shell, with automated axe-core checks in the test suite. Automated checks cover only part of the criteria set.

**Evidence required.** Manual and assistive-technology testing evidence in addition to automated checks. Minimum method: Automated scan plus documented manual testing. Independent audit is required before any external conformance statement.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state that it applies an internal accessibility standard and runs automated checks. It may not state conformance.

**Claim refused.** WCAG compliant; WCAG certified; ADA compliant; accessible

**Note.** Automated coverage is partial by nature. Recorded as PARTIAL rather than IMPLEMENTED for that reason.

### OBL-014 — Internal conformance target version

| Field              | Value                                               |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | World Wide Web Consortium (SRC-016)                 |
| Authority type     | standard                                            |
| Citation           | WCAG 2.2, W3C Recommendation                        |
| Locator            | https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/                       |
| Source version     | 2.2                                                 |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                          |
| Jurisdiction       | NOT-JURISDICTIONAL                                  |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-NOW                                         |
| Trigger            | SSLS publishes a user interface.                    |
| Control family     | ACCESSIBILITY                                       |
| Control status     | PARTIAL                                             |
| Evidence status    | NOT-PRODUCED                                        |
| Owning route       | Accessibility validation work package               |
| Review requirement | ACCESSIBILITY REVIEW REQUIRED                       |
| Review trigger     | Publication of any accessibility conformance report |

**What the source states.** W3C states version status and conformance levels. W3C does not impose a legal duty.

**Obligation.** WCAG 2.2 is the current W3C Recommendation and its Level AA criteria form a superset of the WCAG 2.1 AA criteria named in ADA Title II and the HHS Section 504 rule.

**SSLS interpretation.** Targeting 2.2 AA satisfies the 2.1 AA criteria named in regulation and avoids a re-test cycle. This is an engineering decision, recorded as such, and it creates no conformance claim.

**Current phase.** Applies now as an internal engineering target, not as a legal duty.

**Future phase.** Remains the internal target unless a regulation names a different version.

**Required control.** A single declared internal target version applied consistently across the design system.

**Current control.** ULW-AS-001 v1.3 is the internal standard. Its stated relationship to a specific WCAG version is not recorded in a single canonical place.

**Evidence required.** A recorded decision naming the target version and its relationship to ULW-AS-001. Minimum method: Owner decision record.

**Claim permitted.** SSLS may state which version it builds toward. It may not state that it meets it.

**Claim refused.** WCAG 2.2 AA conformant

**Note.** Raised as a decision candidate for the owner because the internal standard and the external version are not yet formally bound.

### OBL-015 — Accessibility conformance report as self-disclosure

| Field              | Value                                                                         |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source             | Information Technology Industry Council (SRC-021)                             |
| Authority type     | market-expectation                                                            |
| Citation           | VPAT 2.5                                                                      |
| Locator            | https://www.itic.org/policy/accessibility/vpat                                |
| Source version     | 2.5                                                                           |
| Verified on        | 2026-08-19                                                                    |
| Jurisdiction       | NOT-JURISDICTIONAL                                                            |
| Applicability      | APPLIES-AT-PILOT                                                              |
| Trigger            | A district or state procurement asks for an accessibility conformance report. |
| Control family     | CLAIMS / TRANSPARENCY                                                         |
| Control status     | MISSING                                                                       |
| Evidence status    | NOT-PRODUCED                                                                  |
| Owning route       | Accessibility validation work package                                         |
| Review requirement | ACCESSIBILITY REVIEW REQUIRED                                                 |
| Review trigger     | First procurement request                                                     |

**What the source states.** ITI describes the template as a reporting template and never as a certification.

**Obligation.** The template is a vendor self-disclosure. Completing it produces an Accessibility Conformance Report, and no accreditation or certification attaches to the process.

**SSLS interpretation.** Any SSLS report must state its testing method and its limits on its face, because a self-disclosure that reads like a certification is a misleading claim.

**Current phase.** Not triggered. No procurement response has been made.

**Future phase.** A completed report will be requested in most district procurements.

**Required control.** A report template that declares method, scope, date and independence status.

**Current control.** None produced.

**Evidence required.** The completed report plus its underlying test evidence. Minimum method: Documented manual and automated testing.

**Claim permitted.** A report may be described as a self-disclosure only.

**Claim refused.** VPAT certified; independently verified accessibility

### OBL-016 — Section 508 procurement standards

| Field              | Value                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Source             | U.S. Access Board (SRC-019)                                              |
| Authority type     | regulation                                                               |
| Citation           | 36 CFR Part 1194                                                         |

| Applicability      | NOT-APPLICABLE                                                           |
| Trigger            | SSLS sells information and communication technology to a federal agency. |
| Control family     | ACCESSIBILITY                                                            |
| Control status     | NOT-APPLICABLE                                                           |
| Evidence status    | INAPPLICABLE                                                             |
| Owning route       | None                                                                     |
| Review requirement | none recorded                                                            |
| Review trigger     | Any federal sales intent                                                 |

**What the source states.** The Access Board states the standards apply to federal agencies and federal procurement.

**Obligation.** Sets accessibility standards for information and communication technology that federal agencies develop, procure, maintain or use, incorporating WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA.

**SSLS interpretation.** Recorded explicitly as not applicable so that it is not mistakenly adopted as the accessibility benchmark. Its WCAG 2.0 baseline is lower than the standard named for SSLS customers.

**Current phase.** Not applicable. Massachusetts school districts are governed by ADA Title II, not Section 508.

**Future phase.** Would apply only on a federal sale.

**Required control.** None at present.

**Current control.** Not applicable.

**Evidence required.** None. Minimum method: Not applicable.

**Claim permitted.** None available.

**Claim refused.** Section 508 compliant

**Note.** Recorded as an explicit NOT-APPLICABLE to prevent scope drift toward the wrong benchmark.
